anchor_comparisons: The counter anchor's 4.48-6.38 band is relevant as a warning against unsupported persistence, but current direct HBM4 sold-out capacity and stable-yield facts support a value above it.

The positive anchor's 18.05-19.0 band is not comparable in durability because current pricing strength partly reflects conventional DRAM and memory-wide scarcity, while planned capital spending and slowing price increases can loosen the cycle.
disagreements: The memo midpoint gives too much weight to memory-wide utilization, inventory and DRAM pricing as if they were HBM-specific bottleneck measurements.
Sold-out planned capacity does not reveal the size of that capacity or the duration and protection of customer allocation.
payload.rationale: All four counterfacts constrain duration: very high conventional-memory margin is described as temporary, large memory capital spending can add supply, second-half DRAM price increases are expected to slow and earnings are said to rely more on price than volume. The positive HBM4 facts establish a current bottleneck, but they do not disclose absolute ASP, stage-level capacity, customer backlog or cash margin. A cyclical scarcity discount is therefore necessary.
payload.why_not_higher: Capital spending, price-growth deceleration and temporary conventional-memory margins can normalize, while HBM stage capacity, backlog duration and realized unit economics remain undisclosed.
payload.why_not_lower: The current record still contains direct HBM4 sold-out capacity, stable yield and product-premium facts, so it is stronger than a weak or unsupported scarcity profile.
